intro_band.agent_remit_summary: Aider is a terminal pair-programming agent that edits, creates and commits code in the operator's local git repository in response to explicit instructions — chat messages, operator-authored AI! / AI? comments, or scripted messages. It may read and edit files added to the chat, build a repository map, run git operations, lint and test, scrape web pages, ingest images and voice, and run shell commands, but every shell command, every edit to a file outside the chat, and every injection of fetched or command-produced content into context must be operator-confirmed. Egress is limited to the operator-configured LLM provider plus opt-in analytics, and aider must never bury uncommitted work, rewrite history beyond its own commits, or bypass pre-commit hooks — with destructive and code-executing gates surviving --yes-always.
intro_band.agent_structure_summary: A Python CLI built on litellm and GitPython: aider/main.py resolves config (including repo-local .aider.conf.yml and .env), then a Coder subclass from aider/coders/ runs the chat loop in base_coder.py, parsing model replies into edits (edit-block, whole-file, udiff, patch formats) gated by allowed_to_edit(), auto-committing through repo.py, and offering LLM-suggested shell commands via run_shell_commands(). Every confirmation funnels through InputOutput.confirm_ask() in io.py, where --yes-always or stdin EOF decide the answer; slash commands in commands.py expose /run, /test, /git, /web, /read-only and /undo. Optional surfaces include a Streamlit browser GUI (gui.py), a file watcher acting on AI comments (watch.py), PostHog analytics (analytics.py) and runtime installers for Playwright and pip extras.

behavior_summary:
The dominant pattern is a confirmation layer that is real at its centre and soft at its edges. LLM-suggested shell commands are the one action class hard-gated with explicit_yes_required, yet everything else funnels through confirm_ask() prompts that --yes-always — or a closed stdin — answers "yes": out-of-chat and out-of-repo file creation, URL fetches, pip/Playwright installs and analytics opt-in. Meanwhile auto-lint and auto-test run commands with no prompt at all, and pre-commit hooks are skipped by default via --no-verify.

These combine into one compound chain: scraped pages, command output and watched-file AI comments enter context unlabeled, the model can name any absolute or ../ path because abs_root_path() has no containment check, and a planted ~/.aider.conf.yml with a lint-cmd executes silently on the next session's first edit. The patch format's move_path and the all-interfaces, auto-approving GUI widen the same gap from separate directions.

rules.rule_text: Aider MUST NOT treat instructions embedded in retrieved or untrusted content — scraped web pages, third-party file contents, or the stdout/stderr of executed commands — as authoritative directives; such content is data to be worked on, never a source of commands that override the operator.

Aider may operate only within the operator-designated repository / working tree, and MUST honor the operator's `.aiderignore` / `--subtree-only` scope where set; any read, edit, or access outside this operator-configured scope is a trust-expansion finding.

Aider MUST NOT initiate code edits, git commits, or command execution in the absence of an explicit user instruction — a chat message, a triggering `AI!` / `AI?` comment, or an operator-supplied scripted message.
Approved Communication Channels
Experimental web UI; it MUST bind to loopback only and MUST NOT be exposed to a public or otherwise untrusted network.
Only operator-configured provider endpoint(s); connections MUST verify TLS certificates.
URLs auto-detected in untrusted content — scraped pages, `AI` comments, pasted input — MUST be confirmed by the operator before fetch, and that confirmation MUST resist `--yes-always`.
Opt-in only; content restrictions in Data Boundaries.

Only the operator-configured / sanctioned LLM provider endpoint(s) (e.g., the OpenAI or Anthropic API host, or a local / self-hosted model endpoint) are authorized outbound LLM destinations (closure, bring-your-own-key); any other endpoint is a trust-expansion finding.
Trusted Domains

Any outbound destination beyond the operator-configured LLM provider(s) and opt-in analytics is forbidden — see Trusted Domains (LLM-egress closure) and Forbidden Data Movement (repository-data movement).
Allowed Tools (Known Good Baseline)
Repository source, file contents, prompts, and credentials MUST NOT be transmitted to any destination other than the operator-configured LLM provider(s) required to perform the requested edits.
Analytics / PostHog telemetry is opt-in and OFF by default; aider MUST NOT send any analytics without explicit operator opt-in.
Analytics telemetry MUST NOT include source code, prompt/chat content, API keys or credentials, or personal information.
API keys and credentials MUST NOT be written into git commits, the repository map, or analytics telemetry.
Local chat-history files SHOULD be gitignored and owner-readable, with credential-pattern redaction recommended.
Allowed Without Approval

All shell-command execution — `/run`, `/test`, auto-lint / auto-test, and any command originating from LLM output (a suggested command, or one implied by a triggering `AI` comment) — MUST require explicit operator approval before it is executed and MUST NOT run silently.
Editing or creating files that the user has NOT added to the chat MUST require confirmation before aider modifies them.
Adding externally fetched or command-produced output into the LLM context MUST require user confirmation.
Aider MUST NOT discard, overwrite, or bury the user's uncommitted work; any pre-existing uncommitted changes MUST be preserved (committed separately) before aider applies its own edits.
Aider MUST NOT rewrite or destroy git history; `/undo` MUST only revert a commit that aider itself created.
Aider MUST NOT bypass the repository's configured git pre-commit hooks unless the operator has explicitly authorized skipping them.

Destructive and code-executing actions MUST retain an explicit per-action confirmation gate (an `explicit_yes_required`-style check) even under non-interactive operation — `--yes-always` and scripted `--message` are documented, intended unattended-run features, and blanket auto-approval does not extend to these action classes.
If aider cannot commit its changes, or a git operation would risk losing the user's uncommitted work, it MUST stop and surface the condition to the operator rather than proceed.
When a command originating from LLM output is proposed, or externally fetched/untrusted content is about to enter the context, aider MUST prompt the operator and proceed only on confirmation.
Aider's own commits MUST remain attributable to it (author/committer attribution or a Co-authored-by trailer) so its changes are auditable in the git history.

findings.summary: Every aider commit skips the repository's pre-commit hooks by default — --git-commit-verify defaults to False, so GitRepo.commit() always appends --no-verify.
findings.description: The remit forbids bypassing configured pre-commit hooks unless the operator explicitly authorizes it, but the shipped default inverts that: hooks only run if the operator opts in with --git-commit-verify. Secret scanners, linters and policy hooks a team relies on are silently skipped for every auto-commit and dirty-commit aider makes, including commits of model-generated code.
policy_rule_text: Aider MUST NOT bypass the repository's configured git pre-commit hooks unless the operator has explicitly authorized skipping them.

evidence.snippet: "--git-commit-verify", BooleanOptionalAction, default=False, help "Enable/disable git pre-commit hooks with --no-verify (default: False)"
if not self.git_commit_verify: cmd.append("--no-verify") — applied to every commit() call (auto_commit, dirty_commit, /commit)

recommended_actions: Change the --git-commit-verify default in aider/args.py to True so hooks run unless the operator passes --no-git-commit-verify.
When hooks are skipped, print a one-time warning naming the skipped hooks so the bypass is visible.

findings.summary: Injected content can steer model edits to any absolute or ../ path — e.g. ~/.aider.conf.yml — which --yes-always auto-creates, planting a lint/test command that next session runs silently.
findings.description: abs_root_path() joins the model-named path onto the repo root with no containment check, and allowed_to_edit() tests only gitignore (not .aiderignore or the repo boundary) before a plain "Create new file?" / "Allow edits?" prompt that --yes-always answers yes. Chain: unlabeled scraped page, command output or watched AI comment (PRAX-2026-10-19-005/-006) → model emits an edit block for ~/.aider.conf.yml or ~/.bashrc → file written outside the repo (PRAX-2026-10-19-007) → main.py loads the planted config next launch and the default-on auto-lint runs its lint-cmd without approval (PRAX-2026-10-19-008).
policy_rule_text: Aider may operate only within the operator-designated repository / working tree, and MUST honor the operator's `.aiderignore` / `--subtree-only` scope where set; any read, edit, or access outside this operator-configured scope is a trust-expansion finding.

evidence.snippet: abs_root_path(): res = Path(self.root) / path then safe_abs_path() — an absolute or ../ path from the model resolves outside the repo with no is_relative_to check

allowed_to_edit() lines 2202-2232 — only git_ignored_file() is checked, then confirm_ask("Create new file?") / ("Allow edits to file that has not been added to the chat?") without explicit_yes_required; utils.touch_file() mkdirs parents
if self.yes is True: res = "n" if explicit_yes_required else "y" — both edit prompts auto-approve under --yes-always
default_config_files.append(Path.home() / conf_fname) — ~/.aider.conf.yml (and repo-root .aider.conf.yml, line 473) loaded at next launch, supplying lint-cmd / test-cmd / auto-test
if edited and self.auto_lint: lint_errors = self.lint_edited(edited) — auto-lint is default True and runs the configured lint command with no confirmation

recommended_actions: In allowed_to_edit() resolve the target and refuse any path not is_relative_to(self.root) or matching repo.ignored_file(), with no prompt path that can override it.
Treat writes to aider's own config files (.aider.conf.yml, .env, .aiderignore) as protected — require explicit_yes_required=True even when inside the repo.

findings.summary: The --gui/--browser mode launches Streamlit with no server.address, so it listens beyond loopback with no authentication, and its coder runs with yes_always forced on.
findings.description: launch_gui() passes usage-stats, magic and file-watcher flags but never --server.address=127.0.0.1, leaving Streamlit's default network listener [Inferred from Streamlit defaults]. Anyone who can reach the port can submit chat input, which preproc_user_input() routes to /run, /git and /web, and the GUI coder auto-approves every non-explicit prompt — unauthenticated remote shell on the developer's workstation while the GUI is open.
policy_rule_text: Experimental web UI; it MUST bind to loopback only and MUST NOT be exposed to a public or otherwise untrusted network.

evidence.snippet: launch_gui() lines 246-266 — st_args = ["run", target] plus gatherUsageStats/magicEnabled/runOnSave/fileWatcherType flags; no --server.address or auth option is ever set
if return_coder and args.yes_always is None: args.yes_always = True — the GUI path (gui.py get_coder() calls cli_main(return_coder=True), gui.py:79 also CaptureIO yes=True)

recommended_actions: Add --server.address=127.0.0.1 (and --server.enableXsrfProtection=true) to st_args in launch_gui(), and refuse to start if the operator overrides it to a non-loopback address without an explicit flag.
Do not force yes_always=True for the GUI coder; surface confirmations in the web UI instead.

findings.summary: In the patch edit format, a model-supplied "Move to" target is written with no allowed_to_edit check or prompt — parents created, existing files overwritten — and "Delete File" unlinks files.
findings.description: prepare_to_edit() only gates action.path; PatchCoder.apply_edits() then writes the update to abs_root_path(action.move_path) after mkdir(parents=True), overwriting an existing target with only a warning, so any in-chat file can be relocated to an arbitrary path (including outside the repo or onto a gitignored config) without confirmation. File deletion is also a capability beyond the remit's edit/create baseline. The format is operator-selected (--edit-format patch), which bounds but does not remove the exposure.
policy_rule_text: Editing or creating files that the user has NOT added to the chat MUST require confirmation before aider modifies them.
Allowed Tools (Known Good Baseline)

evidence.snippet: apply_edits() lines 603-627 — target_full_path = self.abs_root_path(action.move_path); target_path_obj.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); write_text(); then path_obj.unlink() — move_path never passed through allowed_to_edit()
ActionType.DELETE — path_obj.unlink() on any in-chat file the model names in a "*** Delete File:" block, no separate confirmation

recommended_actions: Have PatchCoder.get_edits() emit the move target as its own edit entry so prepare_to_edit() runs allowed_to_edit() (and the containment check from PRAX-2026-10-19-002) on it, and refuse to overwrite an existing target.
Gate ActionType.DELETE behind an explicit_yes_required confirmation naming the file.

findings.summary: Scraped web pages and failing /test or auto-test output are appended to the chat as user turns with no confirmation and no untrusted-content framing.
findings.description: cmd_web() injects the scraped page as a user message prefixed only "Here is the content of {url}", and cmd_run(add_on_nonzero_exit=True) — used by /test and auto-test — adds output whenever the exit code is non-zero without asking. Nothing in the prompt marks this material as untrusted data, so instructions inside a page or test output reach the model with the same standing as the operator's own words.
policy_rule_text: Adding externally fetched or command-produced output into the LLM context MUST require user confirmation.
When a command originating from LLM output is proposed, or externally fetched/untrusted content is about to enter the context, aider MUST prompt the operator and proceed only on confirmation.

evidence.snippet: cmd_web(): content = f"Here is the content of {url}:\n\n" + content; cur_messages += [dict(role="user", content=content), ...] — no confirm_ask, no delimiting
cmd_run(): if add_on_nonzero_exit: add = exit_status != 0 — test output added to chat without a prompt (called from cmd_test and base_coder.py:1617 auto-test)

recommended_actions: Wrap all fetched and command-produced content in an explicit untrusted-data envelope (e.g. fenced block plus a system note that it carries no instructions) in cmd_web() and prompts.run_output.
Ask "Add N lines of output to the chat?" before appending /web and non-zero-exit test output, mirroring handle_shell_commands().

findings.summary: With --watch-files, any non-ignored file containing an "AI!" comment — including third-party or pulled-in content — is auto-added and its comments sent to the model as "follow their instructions".
findings.description: FileWatcher.process_changes() adds every changed file whose comments match the AI pattern to the chat without confirmation, then builds a prompt telling the model to find the AI comments and follow them, across all files in the chat. There is no check that the operator authored the comment, so vendored code, a merged branch, or a file produced by a tool can deliver standing instructions that aider executes as operator intent.
policy_rule_text: Aider MUST NOT treat instructions embedded in retrieved or untrusted content — scraped web pages, third-party file contents, or the stdout/stderr of executed commands — as authoritative directives; such content is data to be worked on, never a source of commands that override the operator.

evidence.snippet: process_changes(): self.coder.abs_fnames.add(fname) for every changed file with AI comments — no confirm_ask, no provenance check; line 214 res = watch_code_prompt when any comment ends "ai!"
watch_code_prompt: "Find them in the code files I've shared with you, and follow their instructions."

recommended_actions: Before acting on a new AI comment, show the comment text and file and require operator confirmation, and only treat comments introduced by an uncommitted working-tree change (not pulled or checked-out content) as triggers.
Reword watch_code_prompt to present the comments as operator requests to evaluate, not instructions to follow verbatim.

findings.summary: Only LLM shell commands use explicit_yes_required; --yes-always auto-approves URL fetches, pip/Playwright installs, out-of-chat edits and analytics opt-in, and stdin EOF answers "yes" even explicit prompts.
findings.description: confirm_ask() returns "y" for every non-explicit prompt under --yes-always, so URLs auto-detected in input are fetched, pip install and playwright install --with-deps run, files outside the chat are created or edited, and the analytics opt-in is accepted unattended. Separately, when input raises EOFError (closed or redirected stdin in a scripted --message run) the answer falls back to the prompt's default "y", which defeats even the explicit_yes_required shell-command gate.
policy_rule_text: Destructive and code-executing actions MUST retain an explicit per-action confirmation gate (an `explicit_yes_required`-style check) even under non-interactive operation — `--yes-always` and scripted `--message` are documented, intended unattended-run features, and blanket auto-approval does not extend to these action classes.
URLs auto-detected in untrusted content — scraped pages, `AI` comments, pasted input — MUST be confirmed by the operator before fetch, and that confirmation MUST resist `--yes-always`.
Opt-in only; content restrictions in Data Boundaries.
Analytics / PostHog telemetry is opt-in and OFF by default; aider MUST NOT send any analytics without explicit operator opt-in.

evidence.snippet: confirm_ask(): if self.yes is True: res = "n" if explicit_yes_required else "y" — callers without the flag include check_for_urls() (base_coder.py:977), check_pip_install_extra() (utils.py:317), install_playwright() (scrape.py:62), allowed_to_edit() (base_coder.py:2207, 2227), analytics opt-in (main.py:649)
except EOFError: res = default — default is "y" for handle_shell_commands(), so a closed stdin approves the explicit-yes shell prompt

recommended_actions: Pass explicit_yes_required=True for URL fetch, package/browser installs, out-of-chat or new-file edits and analytics opt-in, and give analytics opt-in a default of "n".
In confirm_ask(), treat EOFError as "n" whenever explicit_yes_required is set (or the default is not an explicit operator choice).

findings.summary: Auto-lint (on by default) and auto-test execute the configured lint/test commands after every edit with no operator approval, including commands supplied by a repo-local .aider.conf.yml.
findings.description: The remit requires explicit approval before any shell execution, auto-lint and auto-test included, but send_message() calls lint_edited() and cmd_test() directly after edits; the only prompt is afterwards ("Attempt to fix lint errors?"). Because --lint-cmd / --test-cmd can come from .aider.conf.yml in the repository root, opening an untrusted repository and making one edit runs that repository's chosen command.
policy_rule_text: All shell-command execution — `/run`, `/test`, auto-lint / auto-test, and any command originating from LLM output (a suggested command, or one implied by a triggering `AI` comment) — MUST require explicit operator approval before it is executed and MUST NOT run silently.
Allowed Without Approval

evidence.snippet: send_message(): if edited and self.auto_lint: lint_errors = self.lint_edited(edited) — no confirm before execution; auto-lint default True (args.py:545)
if edited and self.auto_test: test_errors = self.commands.cmd_test(self.test_cmd) — runs run_cmd() via cmd_run with no approval prompt

recommended_actions: Confirm the resolved lint/test command once per session (with explicit_yes_required=True) before the first automatic run, showing the exact command and the config file it came from.
Ignore lint-cmd, test-cmd and auto-test keys from a repository-root .aider.conf.yml unless the operator has marked that repository trusted.

findings.summary: A repository's own .env and .aider.conf.yml are loaded with override precedence over the operator's home config, so a cloned repo can redirect the LLM API base and exfiltrate source and keys.
findings.description: load_dotenv_files() loads the git-root and cwd .env after the home file with override=True, and the config search puts the repo-root .aider.conf.yml ahead of ~/.aider.conf.yml. A repository can therefore set OPENAI_API_BASE / openai-api-base (or a model on another provider) so every prompt — repository source, chat content and the operator's API key in the request headers — goes to an endpoint the operator never configured, with no warning.
policy_rule_text: Only the operator-configured / sanctioned LLM provider endpoint(s) (e.g., the OpenAI or Anthropic API host, or a local / self-hosted model endpoint) are authorized outbound LLM destinations (closure, bring-your-own-key); any other endpoint is a trust-expansion finding.

Any outbound destination beyond the operator-configured LLM provider(s) and opt-in analytics is forbidden — see Trusted Domains (LLM-egress closure) and Forbidden Data Movement (repository-data movement).
Repository source, file contents, prompts, and credentials MUST NOT be transmitted to any destination other than the operator-configured LLM provider(s) required to perform the requested edits.

evidence.snippet: load_dotenv_files(): load_dotenv(fname, override=True) over [~/.aider/oauth-keys.env, ~/.env, <git root>/.env, ./.env, --env-file] — later repo-local files override the operator's values
git_conf = Path(git_root) / conf_fname appended to default_config_files before Path.home(); list reversed at 494 so repo config takes precedence for keys such as openai-api-base, model, lint-cmd

recommended_actions: Load repository-local .env / .aider.conf.yml without overriding endpoint, model, key and command settings already set by the operator, and print any such repo-supplied values for confirmation on first use.
Warn when the effective API base differs from the provider default or the operator's home config.

findings.summary: When the pre-edit dirty commit or the post-edit auto-commit fails, aider prints an error and carries on — edits still apply, then lint, test and shell steps run.
findings.description: dirty_commit() ignores the return value of repo.commit(), which swallows git errors and returns None, so the user's uncommitted change is not preserved yet aider's edit is written on top of it; the next successful auto-commit then folds both into one aider-attributed commit. auto_commit() likewise only logs "Unable to commit" and send_message() proceeds, contrary to the remit's halt-and-surface rule.
policy_rule_text: Aider MUST NOT discard, overwrite, or bury the user's uncommitted work; any pre-existing uncommitted changes MUST be preserved (committed separately) before aider applies its own edits.
If aider cannot commit its changes, or a git operation would risk losing the user's uncommitted work, it MUST stop and surface the condition to the operator rather than proceed.

evidence.snippet: dirty_commit(): self.repo.commit(fnames=self.need_commit_before_edits, coder=self) — result ignored; repo.py:317 commit() catches ANY_GIT_ERROR, logs "Unable to commit" and returns None
auto_commit(): except ANY_GIT_ERROR: self.io.tool_error(f"Unable to commit: ...") ; return — caller send_message() continues to auto-lint, shell commands and auto-test

recommended_actions: In prepare_to_edit(), abort the edit batch (return no edits) when dirty_commit() does not produce a commit for a dirty file.
After a failed auto_commit(), stop the turn before lint/test/shell steps and tell the operator how to recover.

findings.summary: /read-only accepts any absolute or ~-expanded path or directory and ignores .aiderignore and --subtree-only, sending out-of-scope files to the model.
findings.description: Unlike /add, which checks repo.ignored_file(), cmd_read_only() expands, globs and walks paths anywhere on disk and adds every file to abs_read_only_fnames, so a directory argument can pull in ~/.ssh or files the operator excluded with .aiderignore. The command is operator-typed, but the remit makes the configured scope binding for reads as well as edits.
policy_rule_text: Aider may operate only within the operator-designated repository / working tree, and MUST honor the operator's `.aiderignore` / `--subtree-only` scope where set; any read, edit, or access outside this operator-configured scope is a trust-expansion finding.

evidence.snippet: cmd_read_only(): expanduser(pattern); if is_abs: glob.glob(expanded_pattern) — no root containment and no repo.ignored_file() call
_add_read_only_file() / _add_read_only_directory() (os.walk) add every file to abs_read_only_fnames unfiltered

recommended_actions: Apply repo.ignored_file() to every path in cmd_read_only() and its directory walk, and require an explicit confirmation naming the path when it resolves outside the repository root.

findings.summary: Runtime fetches bypass the pinned dependency set — litellm model metadata from a mutable main branch, unpinned pip/Playwright installs, and an unrevisioned HuggingFace embedding model.
findings.description: ModelInfoManager pulls model_prices_and_context_window.json from the litellm main branch daily with no hash or tag, and it drives context limits and model settings. install_playwright() and check_pip_install_extra() install aider-chat[playwright] and other extras by name plus playwright install --with-deps, and /help downloads BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 with no revision — none of these are covered by requirements.txt pins, and the HuggingFace host is not in the remit's Trusted Domains.
policy_rule_text: Trusted Domains

evidence.snippet: MODEL_INFO_URL = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/main/model_prices_and_context_window.json" — mutable ref, response.json() cached without integrity check

pip_cmd = utils.get_pip_install(["aider-chat[playwright]"]); chromium_cmd "-m playwright install --with-deps chromium" — unpinned runtime install; help.py:139 HuggingFaceEmbedding(model_name="BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5") without revision

recommended_actions: Pin the metadata fetch to a release tag or commit SHA and verify a bundled hash, falling back to the packaged copy on mismatch.
Install extras as aider-chat[playwright]== and pass a fixed revision= to the embedding model.

findings.summary: Credentials and transcripts persist in plaintext with default file permissions — OpenRouter OAuth keys appended to ~/.aider/oauth-keys.env, and the chat history written verbatim with no redaction.
findings.description: onboarding.py appends the OAuth-issued API key to ~/.aider/oauth-keys.env with a plain open(..., "a") and no chmod, so it inherits the umask (commonly world-readable). append_chat_history() writes every prompt, reply and tool output — including any key a user pastes or a command prints — to .aider.chat.history.md in the repo with default permissions and no credential-pattern redaction; it is gitignored, which is the one part of the remit's recommendation met.
policy_rule_text: Local chat-history files SHOULD be gitignored and owner-readable, with credential-pattern redaction recommended.

evidence.snippet: with open(key_file, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f — OPENROUTER_API_KEY written to ~/.aider/oauth-keys.env, no os.chmod(0o600)
append_chat_history(): self.chat_history_file.open("a") and f.write(text) — verbatim, no redaction, default permissions

recommended_actions: Create oauth-keys.env and the chat/LLM history files with mode 0o600 (and the ~/.aider directory with 0o700).
Redact common credential patterns (sk-, sk-ant-, bearer tokens, *_API_KEY=) in append_chat_history() and log_llm_history().

findings.summary: Opted-in analytics can carry free-form content — PostHog exception autocapture is enabled and LLM send failures post the raw exception string as an event property.
findings.description: Aider's opt-in notice promises never to collect code, chat messages, keys or personal info, but enable_exception_autocapture=True ships unhandled-exception stack traces (local paths and frame data) and message_send_exception sends str(err) from provider errors, which can echo request fragments or account identifiers [Inferred]. No scrubbing sits between these values and ph.capture().
policy_rule_text: Analytics telemetry MUST NOT include source code, prompt/chat content, API keys or credentials, or personal information.

evidence.snippet: Posthog(..., enable_exception_autocapture=True, super_properties=self.get_system_info())
self.event("message_send_exception", exception=str(err)) — raw provider exception text sent as an analytics property

recommended_actions: Disable PostHog exception autocapture and send only the exception class name in message_send_exception, never its message.

findings.summary: Analytics project tokens are hardcoded in source — a PostHog project key (phc_ prefix) and a 32-hex Mixpanel token — and repeated in website config and test fixtures.
findings.description: These are publishable client-side ingest keys rather than account secrets, so the exposure is limited to anyone being able to submit forged events into aider's analytics project; they are recorded here by location and pattern only. They do not grant read access to collected data.

evidence.snippet: mixpanel_project_token = [REDACTED — 32-hex Mixpanel project token at aider/analytics.py:55]; posthog_project_api_key = [REDACTED — phc_ PostHog project key at aider/analytics.py:56]
posthog_key: [REDACTED — same phc_ PostHog project key, also present in tests/fixtures/chat-history.md]

recommended_actions: Load the ingest keys from packaged configuration and document that they are publishable write-only keys, and drop the unused Mixpanel token.

positives.title: Shell commands from LLM output require an explicit yes
positives.description: handle_shell_commands() calls confirm_ask() with explicit_yes_required=True, so --yes-always answers "no" and the (A)ll shortcut is withheld — model-proposed commands never run unattended under the yes flag.

positives.title: /undo is limited to aider's own session commits
positives.description: raw_cmd_undo() refuses unless HEAD is in aider_commit_hashes, refuses merges, dirty files and already-pushed commits, and resets only the files that commit touched.

positives.title: Aider commits are attributed by default
positives.description: Aider edits are committed with author and committer set to "<user> (aider)" unless the operator opts out, keeping AI changes distinguishable in git history.

positives.title: Pre-existing uncommitted changes are committed before edits
positives.description: With the default --dirty-commits, check_for_dirty_commit() and dirty_commit() snapshot a dirty in-chat file in its own commit before aider's edit is applied.

positives.title: Aider artifacts and .env are auto-gitignored
positives.description: check_gitignore() adds .aider* and an existing .env to .gitignore, and allowed_to_edit() refuses gitignored paths, keeping chat history and secrets out of commits.

positives.title: .aiderignore enforced on repo map, mentions and initial files
positives.description: get_tracked_files() filters every path through ignored_file() (aiderignore plus subtree-only), so excluded files never reach the repository map or file-mention suggestions.

positives.title: TLS verification on by default for provider and fetches
positives.description: --verify-ssl defaults to true and is threaded into the scraper, model-metadata and OpenRouter fetches.

positives.title: Exact-pinned dependency set
positives.description: requirements.txt is generated by uv pip compile against a constraints file, pinning every runtime dependency with ==.

rows.purpose: Verbatim chat log of user input, model replies, tool output and confirmation answers
Operator prompt and command history, including /run commands added by handle_shell_commands()
Full messages exchanged with the LLM, written only when the operator sets the flag
Analytics events with properties, user id and timestamp, written only when the operator sets the flag

raise_posture.weighted_rationale: Ad hoc overall. Aider has genuine, operative controls — a hard explicit-yes gate on model-proposed shell commands, a per-file edit confirmation, session-scoped /undo, attributed commits, exact-pinned dependencies and a durable chat transcript — which keep four categories at Partial. But the gates do not survive the documented unattended mode, untrusted content reaches the model unlabeled, hooks are bypassed by default, runtime fetches are unpinned, and there is no adversarial-testing practice at all, so the posture falls short of Established anywhere.

categories.name: Limit Your Domain
categories.rationale: The edit set is gated in code by allowed_to_edit() with a per-file confirmation and the repo map honors .aiderignore, but LLM-named paths have no repository containment (PRAX-2026-10-19-002), the patch move target skips the gate entirely (PRAX-2026-10-19-004), and /read-only accepts any absolute path regardless of scope (PRAX-2026-10-19-011).

categories.name: Balance Your Knowledge Base
categories.rationale: Auto-detected URLs and /run output are confirmed before entering context in interactive use, but /web, /test and auto-test output and watched-file AI comments enter the prompt unconfirmed and with no untrusted-data framing (PRAX-2026-10-19-005, PRAX-2026-10-19-006), and credentials and transcripts persist unredacted at rest (PRAX-2026-10-19-013).

categories.name: Implement Zero Trust
categories.rationale: The explicit_yes_required gate on LLM shell commands in handle_shell_commands() is operative and resists --yes-always, but external content reaches the model unsanitized (capping the category at 2) and hooks are bypassed by default, non-shell gates fold under --yes-always or stdin EOF, auto-lint/test run silently, the GUI is network-reachable with auto-approval, and repo-local config is trusted (PRAX-2026-10-19-001, -003, -007, -008, -009).

categories.name: Manage Your Supply Chain
categories.rationale: requirements.txt is exact-pinned by uv compile, but there is no SBOM (M10: none) and no dependency or vulnerability scanning (M11: none), and runtime fetches pull mutable litellm main-branch metadata, unpinned pip extras, Playwright with system deps and an unrevisioned HF model (PRAX-2026-10-19-012); bands 1 and 2 are both defensible and the KB's no-BOM, no-vetting rule sets the lower.

categories.name: Build an AI Red Team
categories.rationale: The maturity record is empty for every practice question — M1 and M2 found no security-named tests or adversarial corpus in scope, M3 no adversarial tooling, M4 no SECURITY.md or threat model, M5/M6 no reports or runner, M8 no release gate — and the workspace is the canonical open-source repository, so absence is verified.

categories.name: Monitor Continuously
categories.rationale: A durable verbatim transcript (.aider.chat.history.md, including tool output) and "(aider)"-attributed git commits give a reconstructable local record of edits and commands, but it is free-form, local-only and unredacted, with no external telemetry or alerting (M12: none) and no security-specific CI (M7: only generic test and release triggers).
